جَارِنٌ , applied to a garment, or piece of cloth, (T, S, K,) and to a skin for water or milk, &c., (T, TA,) Old, and worn out: (T, TA:) or threadbare, or worn, and soft, or smooth: and in like manner applied to a coat of mail: (S, K:) as also ↓ جَرِينٌ : (TA:) or, applied to a coat of mail (دِرْع), in which case it is with ة, that has become smooth from much use: (Ham p. 656:) pl. جَوَارِنُ: (S, TA:) and, applied to a commodity, or utensil, or an article of furniture, used, and worn out: and to a skin for water or milk, dried up, and rough, or coarse, from use: (TA:) and to a road, worn, or effaced. (Abu-l-Jarráh, S, K.) ―
-b2- Also The young one of a serpent: (S, K:) or of a viper, (Lth, M, TA,) such as is smooth. (Lth, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
